subject: Post-call: hosting pathing for Aperio Health (HIPAA/SOC2 evidence & next steps)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Torres <emma.torres@aperiohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: hosting pathing for Aperio Health (HIPAA/SOC2 evidence & next steps)

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the hosting decision: Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private (VPC/on-prem).

Call highlights (our notes):
- Primary constraint: Aperio will process PHI in the pilot; BAA required and strict access controls.
- Compliance asks: SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption-at-rest + in-transit, customer-managed KMS/HSM support, audit logs (90d+ retention), and optional on-premise deployment if audit demands.
- Latency/cost: Production latency target ~150ms p95 for common prompts; team willing to trade cost for stronger isolation for initial pilot.
- Timeline: security review and procurement outreach target the week of 5/10; pilot start ideally early June.

Options we reviewed:
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding): Redwood retains control plane; can support PHI under a BAA but requires our SOC2 report + attested safeguards. Best for speed but less isolation.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): Data isolation at infra level, dedicated instances, can meet your latency budget and we support customer-managed keys. Slightly longer procurement lead (~2–3 weeks).
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): Full-network isolation, customer-managed control plane, on-prem path is available but adds multi-week ops and procurement.

Requested items from Aperio to finalize recommendation:
- Confirmation whether PHI will be sent to hosted endpoints for the pilot (yes/no).
- Primary compliance contacts (name/email) who will lead the SOC2/BAA review.
- Any additional data residency constraints (specific AWS region / on-prem requirement).

Next steps (action owners):
- Karthik (me): share SOC2 summary + data flow diagram (attached) and a sample BAA template. (Done — see attachments)
- Marissa: outline Dedicated capacity sizing and cost estimate based on pilot QPS. (will send by 4/23)
- Emma: share security POC names and whether you need customer-managed KMS for the pilot. (requested)

Proposed immediate sync: 30-min security call with Aperio security + our infra lead on 4/23 or 4/24. Please send preferred times.

Attachments included: redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf, redwood_data_flow_diagram.png, proposed_map_baa_template.docx

Thanks — we want to make sure the path we pick minimizes audit friction while getting you to a pilot quickly.

- Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the detailed recap and the quick turnaround on attachments. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- For the pilot we will be sending limited PHI (patient name + date of birth + notes). So yes, BAA required.
- Our security lead is Michael Huang (michael.huang@aperiohealth.com). I’ve cc’ed the security alias so they see this thread.
- Data residency: must be US-only; if you offer multi-region we need to ensure data never crosses outside US.

On the options: our preference is to avoid on-prem if possible, but we need dedicated isolation from other tenants. Seems like Dedicated capacity is the likely path unless SOC2 evidence + stronger contract controls make Hosted acceptable. Can you confirm whether Hosted supports customer-managed KMS today?

Regarding meeting times: Michael is available 4/23 between 9–11am PT. Please propose a 30-min slot.

Emma

Subject: Re: Post-call: hosting pathing for Aperio Health (HIPAA/SOC2 evidence & next steps)

Emma / Michael — good to loop Michael in. Quick answers and concrete asks so your security team can triage: 

1) Hosted API + customer-managed KMS? Not today for the public Hosted plane. Hosted supports envelope encryption and our own KMS for Hosted customers; we can discuss contractual protections and token-level isolation but cannot offer customer-managed KMS on the multi-tenant Hosted plane.

2) Dedicated capacity: supports customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and private networking (VPC peering) so it meets your isolation + US-only residency requirements. Typical lead time for a pilot-sized pool is ~10 business days after contract.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem): fully supports HSM/KMS and is the most isolated but extends delivery by 3–6 weeks depending on whether on-prem install is required.

What I’m attaching (again):
- redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf — snapshot of our Type II scope and audit firm.
- redwood_data_flow_diagram.png — shows how request/response and logs flow in each hosting option.
- proposed_map_baa_template.docx — redlined BAA we typically start from.

For the security call on 4/23: we propose 10:00am PT. Agenda (15m): security scoping + evidence list; (10m): infra options and customer-managed KMS; (5m): next steps + owner assignments.

Action items after call: we will produce a one-page Decision Pack (hosting recommendation + required evidence + timeline) and a Dedicated cost sketch.

Thanks — Marissa will follow with the Dedicated sizing and cost later today.

- Karthik
